proposition: Ibn Turka's own schemes present the three forms of the letter in different orders: the R. Ḥurūf lists written, spoken, then mental; the Mafāḥiṣ sections run mental, written, spoken; the Persian treatise On Letters, as quoted, runs sight (written), heart or mind (mental), hearing (spoken).

mediation.who: Melvin-Koushki, paraphrasing or translating Ibn Turka's own work
mediation.note: the order is Melvin-Koushki's summary in each case
